01 / THE PERSON BEHIND THE PROJECTS

Hi, I'm Paakhi.

A CSE student who likes understanding how things work — and finding creative ways to express what she sees.

I'm currently pursuing Computer Science and Engineering at Vellore Institute of Technology. I'm interested in technology, practical problem-solving and the process of turning an idea into something that works.

I chose CSE Core because it brings together technology, creativity and career opportunities. I want to build a strong foundation in programming and software development while exploring areas such as artificial intelligence and cybersecurity through hands-on work.

Outside academics, I enjoy taking photographs on my phone and painting. These interests give me a different space to experiment with colour, composition and ideas. This portfolio brings both sides together: the projects I'm learning from and the creative work that reflects who I am.

01 — IN PROGRESS / PROJECT WORK

SafeLab Sentinel

An intelligent laboratory monitoring concept that brings safety monitoring and cybersecurity awareness into one interface.

The project combines a dashboard with simulated sensor readings, device authentication, message-integrity checks, anomaly detection and risk evaluation. It is designed to help users observe unusual conditions and review logged events in a lab environment.

PythonStreamlitFastAPIMachine LearningHMACSQLite
FOCUSSafety + Security
STATUSPrototype / ongoing

02 — CAD / ENGINEERING DESIGN

3D CAD Modelling

Created a dimensioned sketch and developed it into a 3D component using CAD tools. This work helped me practise interpreting dimensions, shaping geometry and moving from a 2D profile to a 3D model.

CADSketching3D Modelling

03 — CIRCUIT SIMULATION

PSpice Circuit Analysis

Built and simulated circuit schematics, then reviewed the displayed voltage and current values. The exercise connected circuit theory with software-based analysis and interpretation.

PSpiceCircuit TheorySimulation

04 — LAB PRACTICE

Electronics Experiments

Worked with a breadboard and laboratory instruments as part of practical electronics learning. The photos document component connections and a circuit setup with an illuminated LED.
